Observed series often use different units from the variables in the solved model.

::: {.lesson-links}
[View notebook on GitHub]({{< meta repo-blob >}}/examples/rank/notebooks/rank_extension_07.ipynb){.btn .btn-outline-secondary .btn-sm}
:::

## Model

So far, we have used variables that we have already defined to solve the model. At the same
time, estimation usually requires transforming the model variables to match them to the
actual observed data. As a next step, we keep the economy of [Extension 6](extension-06.qmd)
and modify our code to incorporate the following observation equation, which expresses the
output gap in percent and annualizes quarterly inflation and interest-rate deviations,

$$
\begin{bmatrix}\text{Output gap}\\\text{Inflation}\\\text{Interest rate}\end{bmatrix}
=\begin{bmatrix}100\hat X_t\\400\hat\Pi_t\\400\hat I_t\end{bmatrix}+u_t,
\qquad u_t\sim N(0,\Sigma_u).
$$

We also increase the measurement error so that $m_E=0.25$ of each transformed series' variance.

## Neural network solution

### Formulation

The policy network still returns deviations in model units. We change the units only in the
observation equation, and the equilibrium residuals keep their original scale.

The loss is unchanged from [Extension 1](extension-01.qmd). It is the weighted mean of the squared residuals $F_1$ (Euler equation), $F_2$ (Phillips curve), and $F_3$ (Taylor rule), with expectations approximated by Monte Carlo shock draws.

### In the code

#### Transform before adding measurement error

We multiply output by 100 and inflation and the interest rate by 400. Then we
collect these values in the observation dictionary.

```{.python filename="examples/rank/rank_extension_07.py"}
def observe(self, obs_raw):
    # New in Extension 7: output gap in percent, inflation and the interest rate annualized.
    return {"X": 100 * obs_raw["X"], "Pi": 400 * obs_raw["Pi"], "I": 400 * obs_raw["I"]}
```
::: {.code-source}
[View in `rank_extension_07.py` on GitHub]({{< meta repo-blob >}}/examples/rank/rank_extension_07.py)
:::

`simulate` returns these transformed observations. The notebook then adds measurement
error with `error_share=0.25`. The particle filter applies exactly the same transformation
to its predictions before comparing them with the data.
